subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.

spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Spears
spec.description: A hulking five-headed hydra in God of War style: blackened scarred hide, bone-white horns and fangs, rune-brands and wounds glowing ember-red, bronze spears and chains still lodged in its flesh.
spec.layout:
A four-legged swamp-reptile titan facing +Z, front to back along z. The torso is a deep barrel (x +-1.5, y 1.5-3.6, z -2.4 to 2.4) with a heavy shoulder hump at the front. Four stout legs stand on y=0, hind legs digitigrade (knee forward, hock back), front legs with elbows back, each ending in three or four big bone claws. A thick tail leaves the rump, slopes down toward the floor and ends in a bone spade-blade at about z=-5.3.

Five necks leave the chest top at z~1.8 and fan out in a rest pose, separated and not tangled, each rising, arcing forward and ending in a head that looks forward and slightly down. Neck A is the centre (x=0, tallest, head y~4.9). Necks B and C are inner left (+x) and inner right (-x), heads at x=+-2.0, y~4.5. Necks D and E are outer left and right, lower and splayed, heads at x=+-3.2, y~3.7. Silhouette from the front is a crown fan: the centre is highest, the outer heads lowest, with a clear gap between heads. The overall profile is a bulky, heavy-shouldered mass with long thin necks. Every head has an upper jaw on headX and a separate lower jaw on jawX, mouths shut or very slightly open, because the rig opens them.

STYLE (God of War, grim Norse/Greek myth): desaturated, cold, battle-worn. Hide is blackened green-grey (dark on top and flanks, dirty pale belly and throat plates underneath). Blocky chunky shapes with faceted low-poly segments. Each part gets broad plate and scale shapes: big overlapping dorsal and neck plates in a hideDark -> hideMid -> hideLight root-to-tip order, never fine noise. Warm accents are used sparingly and glow: ember-red and rune-orange cracks, rune brands and mouth interiors (the builder should use glow() from the glow kit on rune brands, eyes and mouth ember). Wounds, claw-scar slashes and dried blood strips in scarFlesh and blood. Souvenirs of past heroes: broken bronze spears and a lodged axe in the back, iron shackles and snapped chains on the ankles and necks, bronze armour scraps bolted into the hide. Bone horns, fangs and claws are big and clear. Mud and grime go on the feet (hideDark patches), and the belly is paler. Every surface is one flat colour per part; scars, runes, seams, rivets and eyes are small separate parts seated on the surface.

What each part owns is listed under parts. Everything meets at the mounts: necks start at neckBase*, heads at head*, legs at hip*, tail at tailRoot.

parts.builds: The barrel torso and everything lodged in it. One smooth loft/sweep body skinned over hips, spine and chest (belly sags lower and is pale 'belly' colour via sectors; flanks hideMid, back hideDark) with a heavy shoulder hump at the front where the five necks sprout, and a thinner waist to the rump. Exposed rib ridges on the flanks (curved boneDark bars under the hide), a double row of big dorsal bone plates (hideDark root -> boneDark tip) along the spine from the shoulders to the rump (tailRoot), and pale belly plates (rows of flat 'belly' bands). Hide texture as chunky overlapping scale plates in hideMid/hideLight in patches, with mud/grime on the lower flanks in hideDark. Battle damage: three long diagonal claw-slash scars (scarFlesh strips with blood edges), a stitched leather-and-iron cauterised stump scar on the shoulder with glowing ember cracks (ember, glow), and rune brands (small runeGlow shapes of Norse-style angular glyphs, glow) on both flanks. Souvenirs: 3-4 broken bronze spears (bronzeDark shafts, bronze bands, iron heads) at slants in the back and flank, one big double-bladed iron axe (ironDark haft, iron head) buried in the left shoulder, a shattered bronze Spartan-style shield-rim shard bolted into the right flank with rivets, and two iron chains (chain, ironDark links as small torus/box links) wrapped around the chest and snapped, trailing links over the shoulder. Includes the neck-root collars: a thick scarred ring of hide plates around each of the five neck roots at neckBase*, sized to the neck radius (about 0.45 m for A, 0.4 m for B/C, 0.35 m for D/E) so the neck sweeps emerge from them. Belongs to joints hips, spine, chest. It does NOT build legs, tail, necks or heads.
parts.attaches: Neck roots at neckBaseA..E (chest joint). Leg tops at hipFL/FR (chest) and hipHL/HR (hips). Tail begins at tailRoot (hips). Dorsal plates run from shoulderHump to tailRoot along spineTop.

parts.builds: All four legs, standing on y=0 (claws sink up to 0.05 m into the floor). Front legs (FL, FR) elbow-back, heavy forearms, hind legs (HL, HR) digitigrade with big thighs, knee forward, hock back; use limb IK from the hip mounts to the foot mounts. Each leg is a smooth sweep on its joint chain (hip, knee, ankle, toe) with a muscular thigh/upper arm (radius about 0.5 at the hip tapering to 0.22 at the ankle), hideMid on the outside with hideDark underside; scale plates (hideLight edged) stacked down the front of each shin, a spiked knee/elbow spur (boneDark), and a broad four-toed foot with big curved bone claws (claw colour at the tip, boneDark base; 4 toes on front feet, 3 forward plus a dewclaw on hinds) spread out, plus toe pads and mud/grime patches in hideDark on the lower leg and foot. Details: an iron shackle ring (iron with ironDark rivets) around each ankle with a snapped chain stub dangling (chain links); fresh scars; rune bands (runeGlow, glow) on the thighs. The four legs are consistent mirrors (+x left): 2 of each. Belongs to joints hipFL..toeHR.
parts.attaches: Tops meet the torso underside at hipFL/FR and hipHL/HR (the leg radius at the hip should overlap the torso). Feet at footFL, footFR, footHL, footHR on the floor.

parts.builds: The long thick tail, a smooth sweep over tail1..tail6 starting at tailRoot with radius 0.6 and tapering to 0.12, sloping down toward the floor and ending in a bone spade-blade. Countershaded: back hideDark, flanks hideMid, underside belly colour (sectors). A row of dorsal plates along the top continuing the torso's row (hideDark root -> boneDark tip) shrinking to the tip, side ridges of hideLight scale plates, banded scars (scarFlesh ring cuts) and ember-glow cracks (ember, glow) between plates. Near the base an iron shackle band (iron + ironDark rivets) with a snapped chain hanging. At the tip (tailTip) a big flat bone spade/blade extrude (bone, with boneDark notched edge, a central ridge, and a runeGlow glyph, glow) plus two side barbs. Belongs to joints tail1..tail6.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailRoot, where the torso rump ends (overlap the rump radius slightly). Tip at tailTip.

parts.builds: The five neck tubes from the chest roots to the head joints, each a smooth sweep skinned over its three neck joints (A: neckA1..A3, B: neckB1..3, C: neckC1..3, D: neckD1..3, E: neckE1..3), starting at neckBase* and ending at head*, where the head's skull overlaps the neck end. Radii: A 0.4 to 0.28, B/C 0.36 to 0.26, D/E 0.32 to 0.24. Colours by place: the back is hideDark -> hideMid, the throat/underside is 'belly' with ladder bands of throat plates. Each neck has a row of dorsal spine plates (hideDark, boneDark tips) and a pair of small side frills. Each neck wears its own history: A has two iron bands with rivets and a snapped chain; B has scarFlesh slash scars with stitching; C has a lodged broken bronze spear tip and a bloody wound; D has a bronze armour scrap bolted on with leather straps; E has glowing ember cracks (glow) and a rune brand. Add neck rings of scale plates in hideLight and a few small bone spikes. Mirror B/C and D/E consistently (+x left). Belongs to the neck joints only (not heads or jaws).
parts.attaches: Roots at neckBaseA..E, which the torso collars surround. Each neck ends at headA..E, where the heads begin; necks stop at the head joint.

parts.builds: All five dragon-like heads, built with one reusable head helper scaled per head (A 1.15, B and C 1.0, D and E 0.9; each head about 1.4 m long including snout, 0.7 m wide), at the headA..E mounts, each facing its joint's dir. Each head is a skull (hideMid with hideDark top) and a blocky tapered snout on the head joint (upper jaw: palate, upper teeth row of 8-10 bone fangs plus two long fangs), and a SEPARATE lower jaw on the jaw joint (jawA..E; chin, lower teeth row, tongue in tongue colour, throat in mouthInner, with a small glowing ember ember (glow) inside the mouth). The mouth is shut or only slightly open. Face: two big angry eyes seated on the sides of the skull (eyeAmber glow, with an eyeSlit vertical pupil and a dark brow ridge hideDark over them for a scowl), nostril holes on the snout tip, a heavy brow ridge, cheek frill of bone spikes, and a pair of large swept-back horns (horn colour with hornTip ends, ringed with boneDark bands), plus 2 small side horns and a short crest of plates down the back of the skull. Individual traits: A is the largest with a crown of 4 horns and a bronze circlet scrap; B has a broken horn (stump) and a slashed cheek (scarFlesh); C has a blinded eye (frost milky eye with a scar slash across it); D has an iron muzzle band with rivets and a chain; E has extra spikes and glowing ember cracks (glow) on the brow. Mirror B/C and D/E (+x left). Heads' parts ride headX (skull, upper jaw, horns, eyes) and jawX (lower jaw, lower teeth, tongue). Details seated on the head surface: wrinkles, scale plates, rune brand on forehead of A (runeGlow, glow). Do NOT build any neck tube.
parts.attaches: Each head's back of skull sits on the neck end at headA..E; the jaw hinge is jawA..E, slightly below and behind the eye.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the spec for a five-headed hydra in a God of War aesthetic—grim Norse/Greek styling with rune-carved bronze and iron, red accents, scars, and chains. I'm planning a quadruped body roughly 6 wide, 5.5 tall, and 8 long, with five necks splaying outward into heads in a resting pose, facing forward along +Z.

Now I'm breaking the model into parts: the torso with ribs, scars, chain harness, and spine ridge; four stout clawed legs; a long curving tail ending in a bone blade; and the five necks with scaled ridges. I'm weighing how to divide the heads across build functions since five is an awkward number—considering splitting them unevenly between two part-builders or just handling all five heads in a single dedicated function.

I'm settling on five total parts—body, legs, tail, necks, heads—and sketching a rough budget across them (roughly 190/170/100/180/260), while planning the joint hierarchy: hips and spine as roots, four joints per neck plus head and jaw joints for each of the five heads, three or four joints per leg, six for the tail. I'm now placing coordinates for the torso and spine chain, figuring out hip height and leg segment lengths so the creature's feet reach the floor properly.

Now I'm working out joint placement for each leg, naming hip/knee/ankle/toe chains per side (front legs stouter, hind legs bigger and more digitigrade), assigning rough XYZ coordinates for each joint so the stance looks like a reptilian hydra body.

Next I'm turning to the five necks, giving each an id (n0 center, n1/n2 inner left/right, n3/n4 outer left/right), setting their base coordinates spread across the chest, and planning a rising, arcing rest pose for them.

Then I'm placing the heads at the end of each neck: center head front-up, inner heads slightly lower and spread, outer heads widest and lowest. I'm checking the overall creature dimensions, settling on roughly 7 wide, 5.8 tall, 10 long, with z spanning -5 to 5.

I'm naming the five necks A through E (center, inner-left, inner-right, outer-left, outer-right), each with three joints plus a head, and working out coordinates for neck A's base, midpoints, and head position.

Still plotting neck coordinates...

Mirroring heads C and E to negative x, varying head heights for a fan shape, and maybe giving one head a scar for character. Now working out the tail path, curving it down from the neck base toward the floor where the tip could rest.

Continuing the tail curve down to z=-5, y=0.35, ending in a spade blade, keeping lateral movement minimal for a rest pose, and deciding the tip doesn't actually need to touch the floor since that's reserved for the legs. Moving on to defining the torso and leg boxes with their rough dimensions.

For style, I'm leaning heavily into a God of War Norse aesthetic — dark ash-grey or blackened green-grey scaly hide, bone-white horns and fangs, rust-red war paint with ember-glow accents in the mouth and cracks, a cold blue-grey palette offset by Kratos-red highlights, and armor made of blood-stained bronze Greek/Norse plates with embedded chains and carved runes.

The body carries embedded broken spears and swords stuck in like trophies, chains, scars, and a stitched cauterized stump, while the heads carry the horns, fangs, eyes, and jaw details. I'm laying out a limited palette of around 24 colors covering hide tones, pale belly, scar flesh, bone, horn, and claw shades to keep everything cohesive.

Rounding out the palette with amber eyes, dark eye slits, mouth and tongue reds, ember and rune glow oranges, iron and bronze metals, chain grey, blood red, frost blue, ink black, and leather wrap brown—tallying up to confirm it lands at exactly 24 distinct colors.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root with spine and chest above it, tail joints branching off hips, hind legs attached to hips while front legs and necks attach to chest, heads capping the necks, and jaws hinging off heads. I'm also working out approximate 3D positions and forward-facing directions for each joint, starting with the hips and spine coordinates.

Still placing leg joints...

Letting the toes touch the floor with claws resting at ground level, then mirroring everything to the right side with negated x-coordinates. I'm naming each joint by role (leg segments, digits) and now moving on to the neck chain, placing neckA1 through neckA3 as they curve upward and forward from the chest base toward where the head will attach.

Head and jaw joints follow, with the skull plus snout forming the head length and the mouth hinging slightly below. I'm then laying out the B and D neck chains as offset mirrors sweeping outward in x, with C and E as their negative-x counterparts.

Now I'm defining bounding boxes for each body part—torso, legs, tail, necks, heads—checking that dorsal plates and spears stay within the torso's upper y bound and that the neck/head boxes extend far enough in x to cover the horns.

For surface detail I'm sketching torso features: a belly plate row, visible ribs at the flank, dorsal bone ridges, embedded broken spears and a lodged axe, chest chains with locks, glowing rune scars, stitched wounds, and shredded Spartan armor fragments bolted to the shoulders, plus blood-streaked cut marks. I'm starting on the legs now, describing muscular thighs and scale texture.

For the legs, tail, and necks I'm working out individual markings: knee spikes, bone claws, a broken ankle shackle, mud near the feet, and rune bands running along them. The tail gets dorsal spikes, ridge plates, a notched bone-spade tip with runes, and its own broken chain at the base, while each neck is given unique scarring -- cauterized rings, embedded arrowheads, bone frill fins, and throat markings that differ from head to head.

Now I'm designing the five heads individually: each gets its own skull shape, jaw, horns, brow, and glowing amber slit-eyes with ember light inside the mouth, but I'm giving them distinct personalities -- A is tallest with crown horns, B has a broken horn, C has a scarred blind eye, D wears an iron muzzle band, and E is spiked. I'm tallying the part budgets (190+170+100+180+260=900) to confirm everything fits, then structuring the compact JSON output with mounts, description, and style notes covering the dark, grimy, ember-lit, rune-covered aesthetic.

Writing joint hierarchy...

I'm figuring out how to build the legs since the joints already exist — I'll use sweep with the existing joint list as the bone chain rather than creating new ones, tracing a path through each joint's position.

For the front legs I'll follow the hip-knee-ankle-toe positions as given, and for the hind legs the zigzag path with the hock angled back, using a polyline instead of a smooth curve so the sweep rounds the corners naturally. I'm also planning the radius taper along each leg, picking a hide-toned color scheme, and layering in extra details like a knee spur spike and shin plates per leg.

Now I'm working out how to place small shin plate boxes along the tube at a fixed angle so they sit on the front-facing side of the limb, then building the toes as capsules fanning forward from the toe joint.

For each toe, I'm creating a tapered rod from base to tip with a dark bone material, plus a curved claw spike at the tip tilted downward, and double-checking that the foot pad and toe geometry stay clear of the floor plane.

Now I'm adding an iron shackle torus around the ankle oriented along the leg direction, with small rivet spheres and a short hanging chain of alternating torus links, then placing a glowing rune band torus around the upper thigh near the hip.

For the thigh rune glow, I'm computing the sweep position and tangent along the leg path to orient the torus correctly, sizing its radius slightly larger than the limb's local radius at that point so it wraps cleanly. I'm also adding scar marks and blood near the mid-thigh, plus mud patches on the lower leg using flattened dark spheres.

Now I'm working out toe pads as darkened flattened spheres under the toes, dewclaws as backward spikes on hind ankles, and elbow spurs on front legs, figuring out the correct spur direction based on whether the knee bends forward or backward for front versus hind legs, and mirroring everything across the left/right sides using signed x-coordinates.

Adding plates and foot details...

Working through the claw tip positioning to keep the drop within the foot volume, then adding a small padding sphere at the base of each toe to smooth the joint connection.

The hind ankle and toe placements look proportionate given their z-offset difference, with the connecting tube angling down and forward naturally. I think the geometry is settled enough to write it out now.

I'm planning the buildNecks function, using the existing joint chains for each neck and sweeping skinned geometry along catmull-rom paths through the base and joint positions.

Writing sweep and plate code...

Now for the scale plate rings, I need to work out the sweep/frame logic along the curve's tangent to place each ring, and since explicit frame literals won't auto-bind to the right bone, I'll pass the bone explicitly as the neck joint.

For each ring, I'm choosing which neck bone applies based on the parametric position along the curve, and deciding how to render decorative iron bands as torus rings placed at specific points along each neck.

Now I'm detailing the per-neck variations: dangling chain links hanging from the band on neck A, alternating their rotation for a swinging look, and planning scar slashes as thin boxes on neck B's surface, figuring out the angle so they read as diagonal cuts along the tube.

Working out the spear placement using the hit direction and tangent offset, with a helper for shaft length, plus blood boxes, a wound disc, and bronze scrap plates with torus-shaped leather straps wrapping the neck.

Now I'm adding rivets to the scrap plate, ember crack details with a glowing zigzag pattern, and a small angular rune brand. I'm also sketching side frills from flattened cones placed along the sweep curve, plus bone spikes jutting out at angles, while keeping an eye on the overall part budget.

I'm tallying up piece counts across dorsal spikes, ladder segments, neck rings, frills, and spikes — the numbers keep running too high when multiplied by five repetitions, so I'm trimming each category down (fewer dorsal pairs, shorter ladder, single ring) to land closer to a manageable total around 180-200 parts.

Now I'm thinking through the tube geometry: adjusting radius falloff between two points, using a linear array for sweep radii, and mapping ring positions along arc-length using the tube's parametric function.

I'm sketching the ring placement logic, orienting items outward around the neck using frame vectors and tangents, then setting up a generic config per letter (A-E) with sign, radii, and history, including side angle logic for outer placement. I'll write this all into code next.

Now I'm adding frills as paired cones at ±90 angles along the neck, scaling them thin for a flattened look, plus ladder bands as thin boxes at the belly angle, and a hanging chain made of small torus links positioned beneath the band with incremental vertical offsets.

Next I'm working out the spear geometry -- computing a direction vector from the surface normal and tangent at the neck, placing a cylindrical shaft embedded in the neck, and planning a jagged iron cone tip further out along that same direction.

Still arranging rune glyph geometry...

I'm thinking through how to build the head joints efficiently, planning to use a frame-based approach that computes its own basis vectors from the direction instead of relying on generic orientation words, so the head tilt stays accurate.

For orientation, I plan to derive left and up vectors from the forward direction using cross products, then convert that basis into a quaternion so head parts can all share consistent orientation. I'm also working out where the head origin should anchor relative to the neck joint and skull length.

Now I'm sketching the low-poly head build: skull as a box, snout as a tapered frustum shape, jaw attached to its own joint slightly below and forward, using simple primitives with flat shading throughout.

Keeping the jaw mostly shut but lowering it slightly to leave a small gap for the glowing mouth effect, skipping complex rig rotation for simplicity. Now I'm placing fang cones along the upper jaw, five per side, interpolating width and spacing along the snout length.

Still writing teeth geometry...

For eyes, I'm placing spheres on the skull sides with slight ellipsoid scaling, amber glow, and thin slit pupils, plus a brow ridge to convey an angry expression.

Still working out the brow geometry... tilting the brow boxes with a roll rotation so the inner end droops lower and the outer end lifts, giving that angry slant, then adding small dark nostril boxes embedded into the snout's front face.

For the horns, I'm sweeping a curved path from the back of the skull outward and upward, tapering the radius from base to tip with a bone-colored gradient, then adding a couple of darker ring bands along each horn using flat cylinders oriented along the path's tangent -- building four horns total for this variant.

For broken-horn B I'm giving the left side a shorter stub with a flat capped tip in bone color, plus small backward-pointing cone horns at the cheeks. I'm also deciding side assignments for mirrored traits -- putting the broken horn on the left and the blinded eye on the right -- and starting the cheek frill as three cones per side spaced along the jawline, pointing outward and back.

Now I'm working out a spike helper that computes a direction vector from local basis coordinates and uses it to orient cones, which simplifies building both teeth and horn spikes with low-poly sweeps.

For the back of the skull I'm placing a crest of small tilted spike plates along the centerline, then sizing the skull box itself with a slightly smaller top panel and brow ridge before considering adding surface wrinkles for texture.

For trait variation A, I'm scaling things up 15% and adding four horns -- a big swept pair plus a taller upper pair -- along with a bronze circlet band across the brow and a glowing rune glyph made of thin angled boxes positioned on the forehead.

For trait B, I'm working out a diagonal slash scar across the cheek using three thin rotated boxes with blood-edge coloring, figuring out the rotation math needed to angle them properly on the side face of the skull.

For traits C and D, I'm planning a frosted eye marking and an iron muzzle band with rivets and a hanging chain, interpolating the snout width at the band's position to size the boxes correctly.

For E, I want to add extra brow spikes and ember crack details.

Now I'm plotting the horn geometry itself: curved sweeps from base to tip using a catmull path scaled by the model's size, tilted back and outward with a slight curl, and bands applied for shading. I'll pull in a glow effect from the kits module and apply it to the eyes, embers, and runes for that extra magical highlight.

Then I'm setting up the head-building function, computing orientation vectors from each head joint's axis so the horns, jaw, and features all align correctly per head, mirroring properly for the side heads so left/right orientation stays consistent across all the dragon's heads.

Still defining helper functions for spheres, applying scale before rotation...

Now I'm checking the jaw's hinge placement relative to the head bone, confirming the offset is small enough to look natural even though the geometry uses its own local coordinates. I'm computing the lower jaw's frustum box dimensions and positions, working out the gap between the top of the lower jaw and bottom of the upper jaw so they align properly.

I'm comparing the skull box's vertical extent against the jaw's position and realizing they overlap at the back, so I'm adjusting the skull's center and height to resolve that, then placing the skull top plate, eyes, and brow at consistent heights.

Now I'm computing the lower and upper teeth as rows of small spikes along the jaw, with their width tapering along the jaw length and their base heights set relative to the jaw and upper mouth surfaces.

Positioning the mouth interior slab, tongue, and a small ember sphere inside the jaw to fill the gap visually.

I'm also adding thin glowing ember strips along the mouth corners for a subtle lip-line glow, plus dark nose bumps above the nostrils and tiered snout-top plates to build out the ridge shape.

Now I'm working on cheek plates along the skull sides and placing the eye socket—using a slightly flattened sphere embedded into the skull with a thin slit-shaped pupil box positioned just at its surface.

For the brow, I'm placing a dark ridge box above each eye and rotating it slightly around the z-axis so the outer end tilts up and the inner end dips down, giving an angry expression, mirroring the rotation direction for the opposite side.

Now I'm defining horn geometry for variant A using control points that curve outward and taper in radius, with a main pair and a smaller upper pair positioned higher and further out for a broken-horn look.

Adding side spikes and cheek frill geometry...

For optional surface detail, I'm thinking about skipping elaborate claw scars but adding generic skull wrinkles as thin ridge boxes across the top of the head, using a slightly lighter shade to stand out against the dark skull tone.

Still building the skull geometry...

Still positioning geometry...

Still placing jaw plates...

I'm adding a blending sphere where the skull meets the neck. Tallying up parts per head, I realize roughly 75 pieces × 5 heads would blow past the 260 budget, so I need to trim down to about 50 per head—counting skull, snout, nose, teeth, eyes, horns, and frills to see where to cut.

Still trimming down counts... reducing teeth, frills, and horn rings to get closer to the 260 part budget across all five heads.

Tallying up the full element count gets me to around 45 base pieces plus traits, pushing the total near 290, which feels like too much. I'm trimming redundant pieces—dropping the ember core sphere since the lines convey it, cutting the nose plates, and removing the ring details—to bring things down closer to 260-280 while keeping the side horns and frills intact.

Writing horn sweep function...

Still working out jaw geometry...

Now I'm placing the upper snout box with its nose-tip position and sizing, then figuring out where to tuck the ember glow lines into the gap between the jaw's top edge and the snout's bottom edge, so they peek through as a side-visible glowing seam.

I'll skip adding a chain for the heads since it isn't needed, then handle the TypeScript types—casting the joint's position to a Vector3 and treating the context and indexed lookups as `any` where the SDK types aren't precisely known.

I need to keep buildTorso compact but solid within my part budget, planning out the body loft across hips, spine, and chest using a bone-weighted station list to control width and height along the way.

I'm sketching station positions from rump to shoulders with varying widths and heights to shape the torso silhouette, including sector-based coloring for belly vs. back regions, and planning to use the body surface for raycasting placement of dorsal plate details.

For plates, I'm thinking of stacking two cone shapes per position (a darker base and a smaller boneDark tip) across nine z-positions and both sides for symmetry. For ribs, I'm planning arcs of boneDark along the flanks by sampling surface hits at varying elevations and side azimuths around each rib's z-section.

For belly bands, I'm casting rays upward from below to find hit points, then considering flat boxes oriented along the normal, but since the belly curves, a straight box would poke out—so I'm switching to a loop sweep along the belly contour instead.

Settling on 5 bands with 3 boxes each (15 parts) slightly embedded to avoid protrusion, aligned to the surface normal. For scale plates, scattering flat cone shapes across the upper flanks with alternating colors, and planning mud patches on the lower flanks filtered by normal direction.

For scars, laying out diagonal slash wounds on both flanks using ray-cast points swept into thin flesh and blood strips, with the blood layer wider and shallower to show beneath the cut.

For the shoulder stump scar, placing a disc shape with a radial ring of leather stitch boxes and iron staples, plus a few small ember-crack glows oriented across the wound edge.

Now I'm adding rune glyphs on both flanks using small oriented boxes to form vertical and diagonal bars...

Scaling down to two runes per flank keeps the part count manageable, and I'll build spears with a helper that places a shaft from a point inside the body outward, adding bronze bands and an iron spike head, with some spears broken off into jagged ends instead of clean points.

I'm figuring out surface hit points to anchor each weapon shaft inside the body, then placing the axe in the left shoulder with a haft and crescent-blade head built from extruded wedge shapes.

Still shaping the axe-head outline...

Now I'm adding iron binding rods and a central boss sphere for the head, then moving to design a jagged bronze shield shard on the right flank, extruded along the body's side axis.

I'm working out the cross product to resolve which direction local z points, confirming it points outward on the right side. Then I'm planning the chest chain as a torus loop wrapping around the chest joint, placing links along the loop tangent for proper orientation.

For the torus links, I'm orienting each piece's frame so its plane contains the tangent direction, alternating a second geometry rotated 90° about Y to vary the look across 22 links around the smallest loop near the chest joint, lifted slightly outward.

Now I'm figuring out a second chain draping over the shoulder, using ray hits down onto the surface to build a path from the top of the shoulder down the flank, ending with a few links left dangling freely off the edge.

I'm now tallying up the part budget across all elements — plates, ribs, belly scales, mud, slashes, stump rings, runes, spears, axe, shield, and chains — and realizing the collar rings would blow past my total budget, so I need to trim counts like reducing chain links to 14 each and scaling back the collar plate rings to stay within roughly 190 parts total.

Building collar rings around the neck with a torus sweep, then adding tilted plate spikes around each ring for a layered armored look.

Wait, I realize the body top is actually around 3.6, so placing collars at y=3.0 would bury them inside the hump. I need to recompute the body center and height so the torso spans roughly 1.4 to 3.6, then figure out where the neck ring should exit the surface along its direction vector rather than sitting buried at the base.

I'll find the exit point by casting a ray from a point past the neck direction back toward the base, using the skin surface's intersection to locate the true collar center -- a more robust approach than guessing offsets. Then I'm laying out body cross-section stations along z, each with a center height, width, and depth, tapering from the hips through the belly and up through the shoulder hump before narrowing again near the head.

For the belly sag I'll apply a slight downward shift, keeping stations within the bounding box limits so nothing clips.
